summary: An Indologist and linguist, Constantin D. Georgian studied at Bucharest, the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Leipzig (Ph.D.), learning under Bergaigne, Bréal, Curtius, Leskien, Hübschmann, Brockhaus, and Weber. He taught Sanskrit at Bucharest (1877–1879) and Romanian at Academie für moderne Philologie.

id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
summary: Active in history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology, Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney, served as Professor of History at the École Normale Supérieure (~1794–1795) and studied under Alexander Hamilton (~1802–1803).

Working in Indology, linguistics, and Tibetology, Constantin Régamey earned degrees at Warsaw and studied under Schayer, Turczyński, Przyluski, and Lalou. He held posts at Warsaw, Lausanne (professor 1948–1977), and Fribourg (professor 1946–1977), and served as Swiss Asia Society president.
Constantine Borissoff specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Far Eastern Federal University, Birkbeck, University of London, and SOAS University of London.

Cora Du Bois studied at Barnard College and UC Berkeley. She held positions at Hunter College (~1937–1939), the Office of Strategic Services (~1942–1945), the U.S. Department of State (~1945–1950), and Harvard University (~1954–1969).

Cora Vreede-de Stuers earned a Ph.D. at the University of Paris, where she also worked as a librarian (1932–1936). She later worked as a librarian in Batavia and Indonesia, and lectured in cultural anthropology at the University of Amsterdam (1969–1973).

Working in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, Corinna May Lhoir pursued studies at Ghent University and the University of Hamburg. At Hamburg, she is attested as a lecturer and program coordinator for yoga studies in 2026.

Corneille Jest was a researcher in Tibetology and archaeology. He studied at Paris Descartes University and under André Leroi-Gourhan, and he worked at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique from ~1956 to 1995.

Active in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Cornelis Jan Kuiken earned his Ph.D. from the University of Groningen in 2002. He studied under supervisors Timothy Hugh Barrett, Jan N. Bremmer, and Jaap den Hollander.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Amsterdam and the Remonstrant Seminary, he was a Remonstrant professor (1873) and Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University (1877–1901).

id: P:Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden
summary: An Indologist, Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden completed his Ph.D. at Utrecht University in 1954 under the supervision of Jan Gonda.
Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Corrado Pensa studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He was a professor at Sapienza University of Rome, attested in 1971.
Cortland Dahl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Courtney Bruntz specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a professorship at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and has served as a professor and director at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, Craig Jamieson has been a fellow at Queens' College and served at the University of Cambridge, including as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).
Craig Preston specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Cristina Pecchia earned a Ph.D. from Sapienza University of Rome under Gnoli, Torella, and Pensa, and studied under Steinkellner at Vienna. She has held posts at IKGA and the University of Vienna.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She served as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1999–2012) and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2001–2016).

An Indologist, Csaba Dezső studied at Eötvös Loránd University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2003.

An Indologist, Csaba Kiss earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2003–2009). He was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2019–2024) and visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.
